_meta.note: Each figure carries a source URL and retrieval date. 'derived' marks numbers computed here from official microdata rather than published as such. null means not found in an official or primary source.

source.name: US DOT Office of Aviation Analysis, Domestic Airline Consumer Airfare Report, Table 1 (Top 1,000 Contiguous State City-Pair Markets), via DOT open-data API
source.quarter: 2026 Q1 (latest quarter in the dataset; dataset rows updated 2026-09-03)

definitions.fare: Overall average market fare paid by all fare-paying passengers in the city-pair market, both directions, all carriers. Includes first-class fares paid, excludes free/award tickets (dataset description). Nominal US dollars.
definitions.basis: Treated as a one-way (directional) fare with round trips split in half, per the DB1B-based DOT report convention. The dataset page does not restate this: medium-high confidence.
definitions.nonstopMiles: Nonstop market distance in statute miles
definitions.paxPerDay: Average one-way passenger trips per day
definitions.markets: City markets pool airports. BTS 'New York City, NY (Metropolitan Area)' pools JFK, LGA, EWR and others; Washington DC (Metropolitan Area) pools DCA/IAD/BWI; Los Angeles, San Francisco, Miami, Boston and Atlanta are also metropolitan-area markets; Chicago pools ORD/MDW; Dallas/Fort Worth pools DFW/DAL. The dataset does not list member airports, so these lists come from DOT's city-market convention.

domesticFares.coverage: All 66 pairs among the 12 requested cities appear in the Q1 2026 top-1,000 table.

derivedFromTable1.note: derived here from all 1,000 Q1 2026 markets, passenger-weighted

domesticFares.uncertainty: Quarterly averages from a 10% ticket sample. Individual fares vary widely with booking lead time and season. Q1 is a low-demand quarter.

latestQuarter.basis: BTS itinerary fare, inflation-adjusted to the release quarter
latestQuarter.note: Down 0.02% from Q1 2026 ($436.45 inflation-adjusted). Highest Q2 on record.
latestQuarter.uncertainty: bts.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches, so the figures come from the release text as indexed by search. Medium-high confidence.

previousQuarter.note: As first released: up 4.7% from the Q4 2025 inflation-adjusted $409. The Q2 release later restated Q1 as $436.45 in Q2 dollars.

annual2025.comparison: Down 1.8% from the 2024 inflation-adjusted $394, and 39.0% below the 2000 high ($634 inflation-adjusted)

nationalAverage.methodology: BTS itinerary fare is the total fare per itinerary, with a round trip counted once at full price. It includes taxes and fees at purchase and excludes bag and other ancillary fees and award tickets. Not directly comparable with the DOT Table 1 per-direction market fares.

arcDomesticRoundTrip.note: Tickets settled through ARC (travel agencies) only; round-trip itineraries entirely within the US

laterMonthsFromSearchOnly.uncertainty: from search snippets of the ARC monthly releases; the releases themselves were not opened

nationalAverage.domesticYieldNote: No industry-wide A4A or BTS domestic yield figure was found in a source that could be opened. A4A's fares-and-fees dataset is an interactive exhibit, and A4A's 'State of U.S. Commercial Aviation' deck has no yield figure. At carrier level, search results give American Airlines consolidated yield as 20.21 cents (Q1 2025) and 19.96 cents (Q2 2025); these were not checked against AA's filings. domesticFares.derivedFromTable1.centsPerMile (23.36) is a fare-per-nonstop-mile proxy.

internationalFares.note: No official source publishes average transatlantic or transpacific economy fares by route. The BTS/DOT fare products (DB1B, Consumer Airfare Report) cover domestic travel only. The UK CAA passenger survey does not publish fares, and ARC's public releases give domestic prices only.

derivedPassengerRevenuePerODPassengerUSD.note: derived here as passenger revenue divided by O-D passengers, across all markets and cabins, excluding ancillary revenue. It is a global average per one-way journey, not an economy transatlantic fare.

internationalFares.uncertainty: High. No official per-mile figure exists to anchor transatlantic or transpacific economy fares. Any per-mile value the simulation uses would be a modeled estimate and should be labelled as one.

source.name: BTS Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987-present), monthly microdata covering every reported domestic flight
source.method: derived here by aggregating every row. On time means arriving less than 15 minutes late (ArrDel15=0). Delay minutes are ArrDelayMinutes. Cause shares follow the BTS method: each delayed flight is split across causes in proportion to its cause minutes.

notes: Cause codes: carrier = within the airline's control; weather = extreme weather; nas = National Aviation System (non-extreme weather, traffic volume, air traffic control); lateAircraft = the previous flight arrived late. The weather share in BTS's own charts also counts the weather part of NAS and late-aircraft delays, so it is larger than the extreme-weather code alone.
Cancellation cause codes: A carrier, B weather, C NAS, D security.

The DOT Air Travel Consumer Report PDFs on transportation.gov returned HTTP 403, so the published headline percentages were not cross-checked. They are built from this microdata and should agree to within rounding.
onTime.uncertainty: Low for the counts: this is the full population of reporting carriers, about 7.0M flights in 2025. It covers only BTS reporting carriers (the large US airlines) and only domestic flights.

bagFees.note: First checked bag, economy, one way, standard bag (23 kg / 50 lb). Prices exclude taxes where the airline says so. Waivers for status and co-branded cards are ignored.

carriers.transatlanticEconomyFirstBag: included in Main Cabin (not restated in the 2026 release)

carriers.domesticNote: Applies to Delta Main and Delta Comfort. The page says lower fees may apply depending on purchase date and states no prepaid discount.
carriers.confidence: high (domestic); the transatlantic Basic $75 comes only from secondary sites

carriers.transatlanticEconomyFirstBag: Included in standard Economy. United raised long-haul international (including Europe) bag fees for tickets bought on/after 2026-05-12; the Basic Economy amount was not confirmed.
carriers.source: https://upgradedpoints.com/news/united-airlines-increasing-bag-fees-april-2026/ (secondary; the united.com fee pages did not load)

carriers.confidence: medium-high (official newsroom, read through the search index)

carriers.domesticNote: Main Base, Main and Main Flex fares on US, Latin America, Caribbean and Canada routes. JetBlue says adding bags at least 24h before departure saves up to $10 a bag. Peak pricing applies around holidays and in peak spring and summer.
carriers.confidence: medium-high (the peak/off-peak split was summarised by the fetch tool)

carriers.effective: tickets booked on/after 2026-04-10 (previously $40); prepayment discount removed
carriers.transatlantic: Alaska flies Seattle-Europe routes, but no fee was found for them
carriers.source: https://seattlered.com/transportation/alaska-airlines-checked-bag-fee-increase-2026/4117838 (secondary; the alaskaair.com pages did not render fees)

domesticAndTransborderFirstBag.covers: within Canada, Canada-US, Mexico, Caribbean, Central America

longHaulInternational.covers: Canada/US to Europe, Africa, Asia, Middle East, South America

carriers.transatlanticEconomyFirstBag: Included on standard Economy. Hand-baggage-only 'Basic' fares include no hold bag.
carriers.note: ba.com returned a high-demand holding page. BA prices extra bags per route in Manage My Booking. Secondary sites cite about $75 for a transatlantic Basic bag, but that is a 2020 figure and was not verified.

Economy Light and Basic include no hold bag. The price depends on the route and comes from Lufthansa's baggage calculator; lufthansa.com returned 403. Secondary sites put the transatlantic price at about EUR 65-90 prepaid and a second bag on US/Canada routes at $85; neither was verified.

In Europe every fare except Saver includes a 20 kg bag; the Saver bag price depends on distance band and on whether it is bought online or at the airport. Transatlantic Smart and Flex fares include one 23 kg bag; Saver includes none. aerlingus.com sits behind a bot check. Secondary sites give about EUR 75 online for a transatlantic Saver bag; not verified.

tsa.note: TSA's standing recommendation, repeated in its press releases

checkInCutoffsMinutes.note: Since 2025-06-03 United requires 45 min on all domestic flights (previously 30 without bags). Some foreign airports close earlier: 75 min at Paris and Dubai, 90 min at Toronto and Lagos, per news coverage.
checkInCutoffsMinutes.source: https://www.meetingstoday.com/articles/145248/united-airlines-changes-check-timeframe-what-you-need-know (news coverage; the united.com pages did not render)

checkInCutoffsMinutes.other: Be at the T5 gate 20 min before departure; clear T3 security 35 min before

otherAirports.EWR: metered + $20 Newark surcharge + tolls, including the return tolls

airportTaxis.meter: $3.00 initial + $0.70 per 1/5 mile or per 60 s in slow traffic

fare.area: Downtown (bounded by Alameda St, Santa Monica Fwy, Harbor Fwy and Cesar Chavez Ave, plus Union Station and Chinatown); per trip or group, either direction

airportTaxis.meter: $3.10 flag drop, $0.33 per 1/9 mile ($2.97/mile), $0.33 per 37 s waiting; minimum $16.50 + $4 for trips from LAX
airportTaxis.confidence: medium-high (the rate card is titled 2023; no later card was found)

airportTaxis.note: The GTAA sets flat taxi and limo fares by destination zone. Limos cost about 10% more than taxis, and there is a $15 extra for 4+ bags or an oversize item and $15 for 5+ passengers. Its rate table sits in a JavaScript estimate tool that did not render. Secondary sites put downtown at CAD 60-75 (about 65); not verified.

airportTaxis.includes: Includes the $4.00 Passenger Load Charge. No other surcharges except tolls, clean-up and requested stops; tip not included.
airportTaxis.otherZones: e.g. Kitsilano/Broadway $40, Central Vancouver $35, North Richmond $25

fare.note: metered; no flat fare for a solo ride

airportTaxis.fuelSurchargeUSD: $2.00 when regular gasoline averages $2.90-4.39 over 14 days; $3.00 above $4.40
airportTaxis.meter: $3.50 first 1/8 mile, $0.30 each further 1/8 mile, $1.50 vehicle trip fee, $24/h waiting
airportTaxis.confidence: medium-high (the page's heading reads 'Effective [Insert Date of New Rates]', so no effective date is published)

fare.area: CBD or French Quarter (west of Elysian Fields)

airportTaxis.option: GO Airport Shuttle Connecticut shared-ride van (the same company runs CT Limo private cars)
airportTaxis.timing: First New Haven departure about 03:30, arriving JFK about 06:15. Driving time 90-120 min for about 80 miles.
airportTaxis.discounts: $4 off a round trip; seniors 65+ get $8.50 off each leg (per the search index)

usCBP.note: CBP's Airport Wait Times site gives hourly waits by airport and terminal only through an interactive query and CSV export. No published national or per-airport average was found, and its API could not be reached outside the browser app.

ukBorderForce.note: The standard is that 95% of passengers are seen within the time, counted from joining the queue, and Heathrow reports against it. It dates from the EEA/non-EEA era, and no post-Brexit restatement was found.
ukBorderForce.confidence: medium (confirmed in a 2018 Parliamentary answer; not re-confirmed as current for 2026)

uncertain: domesticFares: the one-way basis of the DOT Table 1 fares is inferred from the DOT report convention; the dataset text does not restate it.
nationalAverage: the BTS 2026 Q2, 2026 Q1 and 2025 annual figures were read from release text indexed by search, because bts.gov returned HTTP 403.
nationalAverage.domesticYieldCentsPerMile is null: no industry-wide A4A or BTS figure was found.
internationalFares: none of the sources checked gives an official per-route or per-mile transatlantic or transpacific economy fare; only IATA global aggregates exist.

bagFees: the United and Alaska 2026 figures come from secondary news because the official pages did not render. British Airways, Lufthansa and Aer Lingus first-bag prices are null; secondary sites' figures appear in the notes only.
arrivalGuidance: United's cut-off comes from news coverage of its June 2025 change.
airportTaxis: the Toronto Pearson flat fare is null. LAX comes from an LADOT card titled 2023. The ATL page shows a placeholder instead of an effective date.
immigrationWaits: the CBP averages are null. The UK Border Force 25/45-minute standard is sourced from government documents dated 2013-2018.
onTime: computed from BTS microdata rather than copied from the DOT Air Travel Consumer Report, whose PDFs returned 403. The two should agree to within rounding.
